subject: Unexpected burst evictions — FinOptics impact summary & remediation checklist
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-17T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Alert: dedicated tenant eviction burst observed affecting FinOptics

Team —

We observed a rapid series of eviction events in the us-west-2 dedicated GPU pool between 08:54–09:05 PDT that impacted three tenants, including FinOptics (tenant id: finoptics-prod). Metrics attached (finoptics-metrics-20280517.csv) show request latency spikes and multiple hot-eviction traces on nodes hosting their reserved slots. Initial triage indicates the autoscaler attempted to reclaim underutilized reserved nodes while concurrent burst traffic caused local memory pressure and vGPU evictions.

Immediate actions taken:
- Isolated affected nodes and marked them DRAINING to prevent further evictions.
- Triggered emergency warm-up of standby nodes for FinOptics’ reserved pool.
- Applied temporary scale-up allowance for their pool to reduce pressure while we fix the autoscaler policy.

Need help from ops and product:
- Karthik: can you validate whether the autoscaler change rolled at 08:45 was the 1-off config push?
- Marissa: please draft a short customer-facing note and hold for Priya’s sign-off.

Attaching the quick metrics export for FinOptics.

— Diego
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Sam Harper <sam@finoptics.com>, FinOptics Platform <platform-eng@finoptics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-17T09:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Alert: dedicated tenant eviction burst observed affecting FinOptics

Sam —

Thanks for the quick heads up while we triage. We’ve isolated the affected hosts and applied an emergency scale-up for your reserved capacity while we complete a root-cause analysis. Short summary for your ops team:

What happened (brief):
- A configuration rollout to the autoscaler coincided with a sudden burst of short-lived concurrency from a FinOptics job, causing local memory reclaim and vGPU evictions on a subset of reserved nodes.

What we did immediately:
- Drained impacted hosts to stop further evictions.
- Brought standby capacity online (warm nodes) for FinOptics to absorb traffic.
- Scoped a short-lived fallback routing policy to route non-latency-critical requests to a compatible hosted model variant while we stabilize dedicated capacity.

Next steps (we’ll own these):
- Full RCA and proposed remediations by EOD tomorrow.
- Runbook and permanent autoscaler policy fix (target: 48 hours).
- Proposed customer credit for the window of impact; we’ll include numbers in the RCA.

We’ve attached a short operational checklist (runbook-dedicated-fallback-v1.pdf) and the metrics export. I’ll schedule a 30-minute technical bridge today at 11:00 PDT unless you prefer a different time — please confirm.

Apologies for the disruption; we’re treating this as an incident with priority P1 for FinOptics.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Account Lead — Strategic Customers, Redwood Inference

From: Sam Harper <sam@finoptics.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, FinOptics Platform <platform-eng@finoptics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-17T09:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Alert: dedicated tenant eviction burst observed affecting FinOptics

Thanks Priya — appreciate the quick mitigation. A couple of asks from our side:

1) Can you confirm the total duration of the impact and how many requests were affected (ballpark)?
2) We’ll need an initial ETA for a permanent fix and the policy change details (what was rolled at 08:45).
3) Per our contract, please include proposed service credit calculation for the impacted window.

We can join the 11:00 PDT bridge. Platform team will also share internal logs.

— Sam
Head of Platform Engineering, FinOptics

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-17T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: root cause & proposed remediation for FinOptics eviction burst

Priya / Team —

Quick RCA summary after digging into the autoscaler rollout and host traces:
- Root cause: an aggressive idle-reclamation threshold introduced in autoscaler config v2.3.1 (rolled at 08:45 PDT) combined with atypical burst traffic from FinOptics' nightly job. The threshold caused the autoscaler to mark some reserved nodes as reclaimable too early, which triggered concurrent host-level vGPU reclaim operations. When the burst arrived, the hot reclaim + influx of new sessions caused memory contention and eviction of tenant processes.

Proposed remediation (immediate):
- Roll back the idle-reclamation threshold change (we have a rollback PR ready).
- Patch autoscaler to respect pinning-hints for reserved tenants during high-variance windows (target patch in 24–36 hours).
- Update deployment gating so a canary is validated against a synthetic short-burst workload before global rollouts.

Customer-facing items to include in RCA:
- Precise impact window: 08:54–09:07 PDT (13 minutes).
- Estimated affected requests: ~1.2k requests across FinOptics production routes (see metrics attachment).
- Proposed credit: 10% credit for the hour that contains the incident; final calculation to be reconciled with billing.

I’ll prepare the technical appendix for the postmortem and coordinate the patch release.

— Karthik
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Sam Harper <sam@finoptics.com>, FinOptics Platform <platform-eng@finoptics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-21T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Post-incident follow-up: FinOptics dedicated pool — timeline, actions, and next steps

Sam —

Following our bridge and internal RCA, here is the customer-facing post-incident summary and concrete next steps. Apologies again for the disruption and thank you for working through this with us.

Summary of impact:
- Incident window: 2028-05-17 08:54–09:07 PDT.
- Affected requests (estimated): ~1.2k requests.
- User-visible effect: transient failures and elevated latency for some synchronous calls.

Root cause (condensed):
- A recent autoscaler config change shortened the idle-reclamation threshold for GPU-backed reserved nodes. The change interacted poorly with a short, high-concurrency job from FinOptics and triggered node-level reclaim operations that caused process evictions.

Actions taken:
1) Immediate: drained affected hosts, brought warm standby nodes online, and applied a short-lived fallback routing to a compatible hosted variant.
2) Short-term (completed): rolled back the autoscaler threshold change within 2 hours of detection; monitor confirmed stability within the dedicated pool.
3) Medium-term (in-progress): patch to respect tenant pinning during burst windows (target deployment: 2028-05-18 22:00 PDT).
4) Long-term: canary gating for autoscaler rollouts and an automated synthetic-burst validator (target Q3 deliverable).

Customer commitments:
- We propose a 10% service credit for the hour that includes the incident (billing team will calculate final amount and post to your billing contact).
- We’ve shared the technical appendix with your platform team and uploaded the full postmortem to the linked drive.
- We will run a joint verification window next Friday at 09:00 PDT to replay a controlled burst with your team if you agree.

Attachments: finoptics-metrics-20280517.csv, runbook-dedicated-fallback-v1.pdf
Related links: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/OPS-1987, https://drive.redwood.com/teams/ops/finoptics-incident-20280517

If this looks good, we’ll route the credit calculation and the postmortem to your billing and security contacts respectively. Let me know if you’d like a follow-up executive summary for your vendor review.

Thanks — we value your partnership and will continue to prioritize stabilizing reserved capacity.

Best regards,
Priya Natarajan
Account Lead — Strategic Customers, Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0123
